refusal_reason: Internally incoherent source (no retraction notice found on page 1 or any of the 21 pages; refusal cites observed defects per doctrine). Document: 'Football Analytics - Using AI and ML to predict the outcome of a football match', student capstone report (Ahuja/Gundu/Agrawal/Kundu, 'Reinventing Business with AI and ML', 2021, sha256 51810ec3502aa6a723fa4870599b48c0f4d8cf54952221b6750eef9e5347f45d). Observed defects, all verified against the extracted text layer: (1) Physically impossible claims: AdaBoost 3-class soccer full-time-result accuracy reported as 97% (p16), rising to 98% under 20-fold CV (p17), 99% on separate train/test (p19), and '99.6% accuracy in Away and Home win situations' (p19). Genuine pre-match soccer outcome prediction caps near 50-55%; monotonic accuracy inflation across validation schemes is a target-leakage signature, corroborated by p4 removing 'HomeWin and ScoreDraw columns due to the high correlation' with target FTR and the authors' own p19 admission 'we might be cautious of Overfitting'. (2) Duplicated filler: the EDA definition paragraph appears twice near-verbatim on p2 ('Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is an observational step...' and 'An observational step known as Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)...'). (3) Nonsense mathematics: p10 states 'M = x1, N=y2, ax + by = c defines the linear span of the regularisation terms', which is semantically meaningless; the document contains no genuine equations, theorem statements, exact assumptions, or breakdown regimes anywhere. (4) Odds contamination: betting odds are explicit model inputs (p2 'betting odds and team strength before each match'; p14 odds columns 'BbMx.2.5 and BbMx.2.5.1' with correlation -0.941), violating the no-sportsbook-odds doctrine, so no reported accuracy may calibrate GSE telemetry. (5) All result tables and confusion matrices are embedded screenshots, not verifiable text. No durable standard math kernel exists to salvage. Honest refusal: never launder manipulated content into the corpus.
